biography.background: Born June 23, 1974, in Laredo, TX. Son of educators Cayetano Tijerina III and Rosalinda Flores. Drafted 8th round by Milwaukee Brewers (1993). Rancher and businessman. Elected Webb County Judge as a Democrat in 2014; re-elected 2018 (76.3%) and 2022 (100% of Democratic primary, unopposed in general). Switched from Democratic to Republican Party on December 10, 2024, announced live on Fox & Friends. Announced congressional campaign December 2, 2025, after timing the announcement to avoid triggering Texas's resign-to-run law (which would have required him to vacate the county judgeship).

countyJudgeRecord.summary: Served as Webb County's chief elected executive 2015–present (11 years). Key county-level actions documented:

keyActions.description: Signed one of the strictest shelter-in-place orders in South Texas, ordering Laredo residents and Webb County to shelter in place beginning March 2020.
keyActions.notes: Enacted against the broader grain of Texas Republican governance at the time. Now frames his party switch partly around opposing such mandates, though his own record implemented them.

keyActions.action: Mask mandate for county government offices
keyActions.description: Maintained mask mandates for county government offices despite Gov. Greg Abbott's executive order prohibiting state and local government entities from requiring masks.
keyActions.notes: Documented by Washington Examiner as part of 'liberal past' framing. Conflicts directly with current party affiliation's stance on mask/vaccine mandates.

keyActions.action: Expanded voting access prior to 2022 elections
keyActions.description: Prioritized expanding access to voting ahead of the 2022 elections, even as Texas Republicans were tightening voter integrity rules statewide.
keyActions.notes: Documented by Washington Examiner. Contradicts typical Republican stance on election administration.

keyActions.action: Defended election officials after ballot recount discrepancy
keyActions.description: Defended election officials following a recount discrepancy involving roughly 300 ballots in Henry Cuellar's 2024 reelection race.
keyActions.notes: Defended Democratic-aligned election officials. Switched to Republican two months later.

keyActions.description: Oversaw construction of Bridge 4/5 and advanced the 5th international bridge project. Also renovated county fairgrounds.

Elected Chairman of TBC in December 2024. TBC advocates for 'fair and effective immigration reform that strengthens borders and recognizes the economic contributions immigrants make to the U.S.' Stepped down upon congressional campaign launch.

endorsements.notes: Trump posted on Truth Social: 'Tano's views are stronger, better, and far less tainted than Henry's, and he has my Complete and Total Endorsement.' Endorsement came after Trump pardoned Cuellar in Dec. 2025 on federal bribery charges but was disappointed by Cuellar's continued Democratic candidacy.

keyExchanges.quote: Over the years, I've watched the Democratic Party shift further and further to the left, and leaving the values that I hold dear to my heart. I've always been a conservative, and the radicalization of the national Democrats pushed me away a long time ago. For that reason, I'm proud to announce I will be leaving the Democratic Party and joining the Republican Party.
keyExchanges.notes: Made the party-switch announcement live on Fox & Friends. Cited immigration/border, oil and gas industry threats, transgender women in sports, and 'woke movements' as specific concerns.

positionConflicts.conflict: As Webb County Judge (2020–2021), Tijerina imposed some of the strictest COVID-19 shelter-in-place and mask mandate orders in South Texas, defying GOP Gov. Abbott's order banning mask mandates in government buildings. He now campaigns as a Republican aligned with those who opposed such mandates, and cited 'woke policies' as a reason for his party switch. His own COVID-era record stands in direct tension with his current political identity.

Prioritized expanding voting access ahead of 2022 elections while Texas Republicans were tightening voting rules statewide. Defended election officials after a ballot recount discrepancy in November 2024. Switched to the Republican Party two months after that defense.

As Texas Border Coalition chairman (Dec. 2024 – Dec. 2025), Tijerina led an organization that advocates for recognizing 'the economic contributions immigrants make to the U.S.' and 'fair immigration policies.' His current Republican campaign focuses on border security and supporting Trump's enforcement agenda. The TBC framing is more pro-immigrant than his current political messaging, though the two are not necessarily incompatible.

A federal election complaint (filed Nov. 2025) alleged Tijerina operated an exploratory committee beyond legal limits to avoid triggering Texas's resign-to-run law. He timed his formal December 2 announcement to remain in the county judgeship through the end of his term (Dec. 31, 2026). Tijerina denied wrongdoing. The complaint was filed by Cecilia Martinez, a San Antonio resident, former journalist, and professor.

raceContext.districtDescription: Runs from San Antonio to the Texas-Mexico border; covers all of Webb County (Laredo). Majority-Hispanic district.
raceContext.cookPVI: R+2 (heading into 2026; was D+3 heading into 2024)
raceContext.pviNotes: One of the most dramatic partisan shifts in the country. Trump won Webb County in 2024 — the county had been reliably Democratic for generations. Webb County saw the fourth-largest swing toward Trump since 2016, a swing of more than 50 percentage points from its previous Democratic baseline.
raceContext.primaryOpponent: Eileen Day (Republican, political newcomer; focuses on stray animal populations and border/poverty interconnections)
raceContext.likelyGeneralOpponent: Henry Cuellar (D, incumbent; federally indicted for bribery, pardoned by Trump Dec. 2025; still running as Democrat)
